🌎 BEYOND THE 956

Colorado native and Fairview High School graduate Jessica Watkins voted from space on Tuesday, November 3, 2026.

Watkins, a NASA astronaut aboard the International Space Station, cast her ballot in the U.S. midterm elections from about 250 miles above Earth, along with fellow American crew members Anil Menon and Luke Delaney.

Menon said in a video posted on Tuesday that all three American crew members had voted, filling out an electronic ballot and sending it securely to election officials. Menon said his ballot was sent to Harris County, Texas, home to NASA's Johnson Space Center.

Colorado Governor Jared Polis highlighted Watkins' vote in a post on Tuesday, noting that if she can vote from the International Space Station, voters on the ground can get their ballots in too.

U.S. astronauts have been able to vote from space since 1997, when Texas passed a law allowing it. Ballots are encrypted and can be opened only by the astronaut and the authorized election official.

Menon reached the station on July 14, 2026, aboard a Russian Soyuz spacecraft. Watkins and Delaney launched on October 1, 2026, aboard a SpaceX rocket.

Sources: Colorado Governor Jared Polis, Facebook post November 3, 2026; astronaut Anil Menon, video posted November 3, 2026, as reported by The Times, Associated Press, and Fox News.
